title: Iran’s Guards Say Two Oil Tankers Hit Mines and Caught Fire Near Hormuz; Claim Unconfirmed
dek: The IRGC Navy says two tankers that switched off tracking systems struck mines south of the Strait of Hormuz. No ship names, flags or casualties have been published, and the claim has not been independently confirmed.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Topographic map of the Strait of Hormuz

keyPoints: Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz, Anadolu and TASS reported.
The statements did not name the vessels, their flags or any casualties, AFP reported.
AFP reported the claim had not been independently confirmed, and UKMTO had not confirmed the incidents when AFP filed.
A separate Iranian Armed Forces navy statement said a third tanker, east of the strait, caught fire after hitting a mine, ANI reported.

CENTCOM’s Oct. 28 statement says the main transit lanes are mine-free and predates the Nov. 13–14 claims. A CENTCOM post Meridian retrieved calls an IRGC supertanker mine claim “FALSE”; the page shows no date.
body:
Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire south of the Strait of Hormuz. The statements were reported on Friday and again early Saturday. The claim has not been independently confirmed. The sources Meridian reviewed name no vessels, flags, owners or casualties, and the U.S. has not issued a specific response to these tanker claims.

## What Iran said

The IRGC Navy’s public relations office said two oil tankers attempted to pass through the strait by an unauthorized route with their navigation and automatic identification systems switched off, Anadolu reported. The statement said the vessels hit sea mines, causing explosions and large fires. It also said one of the ships was a supertanker, and that flames lit the strait’s southern shores.

The IRGC posted a similar account on its Telegram channel, TASS reported. The vessels “hit sea mines, which led to explosions and fires,” the statement said. The navy also warned shipowners against transiting the waterway without coordinating with its maritime traffic control center.

Iranian state broadcaster IRIB said two other tankers that were trying to pass through secretly turned back after warnings from the IRGC’s Naval Traffic Control Center, ANI reported. A separate statement from Iran’s Armed Forces navy said another tanker east of the strait caught fire after striking a mine.

## What has not been confirmed

AFP reported that the claim had not been independently confirmed. It also reported that the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) had not confirmed Saturday’s incidents when AFP filed its report, according to GSM News, which carried the AFP account. Meridian could not find an independent account of the explosions or fires in the sources it reviewed.

UKMTO has reported other incidents in the strait recently. Anadolu reported that UKMTO said on Thursday that a tanker had been struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the waterway.

## U.S. response

Central Command has said that “all internationally recognized primary transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz have been cleared of sea mines by US forces and remain so.” That statement, posted on X on Oct. 28 and reported by Gulf News, predates the Nov. 13 and 14 claims. Gulf News noted that CENTCOM did not identify the incidents it was disputing. A CENTCOM social media post that Meridian retrieved calls an IRGC claim that a supertanker struck two mines “FALSE” and says “No ships have hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz.” The retrieved page shows no date, and Meridian has not confirmed that it refers to the Nov. 13–14 claims. Meridian found no other CENTCOM statement addressing them.

Separately, CENTCOM said its forces intercepted two Iranian attack drones headed toward Bahrain and reported no injuries or damage, Anadolu reported. The IRGC had claimed to have destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain. CENTCOM denied that claim. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard also said it shot down a U.S. MQ-1 drone over Qeshm Island, according to Anadolu. Meridian has not independently verified that claim.

## Context

In a briefing to the UN Security Council on Nov. 13, Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Khiari said the International Maritime Organization had recorded 134 confirmed incidents in the Strait of Hormuz and the wider Middle East maritime area as of Nov. 11, GSM News reported.
